options.text: A substance that is itself oxidised during a reaction
A substance that always contains oxygen
A substance that oxidises another substance and is itself reduced
A substance that prevents oxidation from occurring

questions.explanation: An oxidising agent is a substance that causes another substance to be oxidised. In doing so, the oxidising agent itself is reduced (it gains electrons). For example, in the thermite reaction, Fe₂O₃ is the oxidising agent because it oxidises aluminium while being reduced itself.
